title: "add the ability to generate ui examples to question me skill the question me skill should have the option of image questions. This will require in general settings having the option to save an api key for image gen. For now just implement the muse/meta image gen interface (but we will want to extend it later) . Then on the skill config we should have a image gen dropdown which allows for none, where it remvoes the section for image gen entirely, or  select from availble providers.  the agent/runner will just provide up to 4 detailed descriptions that will be generated example UI's on the survey. The selected answer being saved as an image in the task folder to be referenced (with a reference in the SURVEY.md or equivalent). The idea is the agent can propose some UIs or some logos or similar, then the agent can work to that as a design. We will need to store the key in the backend as we wont want to hand it out, so itll be up to you to determine if it should act as a gateway and the runners should generate images or whether the backend does it. whatevers easiest and most reliable"

# Goal
# add the ability to generate ui examples to question me skill

the question me skill should have the option of image questions. This will require in general settings having the option to save an api key for image gen. For now just implement the muse/meta image gen interface (but we will want to extend it later) . Then on the skill config we should have a image gen dropdown which allows for none, where it remvoes the section for image gen entirely, or  select from availble providers. 

the agent/runner will just provide up to 4 detailed descriptions that will be generated example UI's on the survey. The selected answer being saved as an image in the task folder to be referenced (with a reference in the SURVEY.md or equivalent).

The idea is the agent can propose some UIs or some logos or similar, then the agent can work to that as a design. We will need to store the key in the backend as we wont want to hand it out, so itll be up to you to determine if it should act as a gateway and the runners should generate images or whether the backend does it. whatevers easiest and most reliable

Standards.md`.\n1|# Values\n2|\n3|## User understandable over technical language\n4|\n5|I feel like code should always be understandable by users as they are the ones who dictate process. So the goal of code should make it the most understandable with zero context as possible\n6|\n7|### Principles\n8|\n9|- Long variables names where needed to be descriptive\n10|- Avoid using technical language such as “factory” or “barrel”\n11|- Stick to a common language profile, (tasks always being tasks, stages always being stages etc)\n12|- File structure should reflect the call stack\n13|- Use of JSDocs to explain variables in pure english\n14|- Include why things are done not just what is done\n15|- Use a labelled data inport pattern (IE  `({varA , varB}) => {}`)\n16|- NEVER MENTION DESIGN PATTERNS\n17|- Use @example tags in js doc to easily explain functionality\n18|  \n19|  \n20|\n21|## Functional over Object oreintated\n22|\n23|Although pure functional code can tend to insanity it is always important to note co-mingle state and functionality. Where possible state should leave in clearly defined places, and functions should show a clear line in how we move from one state to another. Traditional object oriented design mainly serves to gatekeep devs(or for game dev).\n24|\n25|### Principles\n26|\n27|- Try and avoid using classes where possible\n28|- Currying can be used to create sudo classes, avoid that\n29|- Functions should follow black box mentality, clear input delivers the same output with no side affects\n30|- Treat variables as immutable unless they are clearly defined states.\n31|- Functions should always be named with a verb in, as they are doing something\n32|- Give the miniumn data to each function as possible. Pick off fields before invocation.\n33|- Each function should only work to achieve its task, with a single responsibility\n34|\n35|\n36|## Co-location over abstraction\n37|\n38|Although abstraction is an essential part of coding it should always only be done by business level intent, not just on functionality. Ideally if you pick a random file in the codebase you should only need to look at the one folder above it and one folder under it to get all the context on its functionality.\n39|\n40|### Principles\n41|- Unit tests should always be placed next to the relevant file\n42|- Generally functions called in a higher function should be placed in a folder of that functions name. IE if `funA.js` calls `funB.js` it should be `./funA/funB.js`\n43|- Generic/helper functions should only be made if they are repeatedly doing the same thing.\n44|- Helpers should be treated like react state and exist at the lowest level folder that is common in the hierarchy of the folders\n45|- If abstracting it would take up more lines/characters than just embedding that line directly on a per file basis avoid doing it. IE don’t abstract a single line just because its repeated unless it has some complex logic like a regex.\n46|- Don’t fear repetition of code\n47|- Make sure the code is easily searchable for any given task. If I said modify the task history box in the ui it should  be easy and logical to figure out where that is.\n48|- Use folders as a tool for organising\n49|\n50|## Tested over trusted \n51|\n52|Functionality should not assumed to exist until it is tested and evidenced. “it should work” isn’t always reliable and we want to make sure there are no regressions. \n53|\n54|### Principles\n55|- Try and at least plan what tests you are going to make before you  code a function\n56|- Don’t assume typing is correct until proven, or allow it to fail safe\n57|- Failures should clear transparent and observable, every function doesnt need to intensly check it just needs to report failures accurately\n58|- Tests must be consistent\n59|- Integration test must reflect how a user could want to use the app\n60|- Use the lowest possible level of tests( Ie Unit over api over e2e) for the fastest test cycle\n61|\n62|\n63|## Fast iteration over long planning\n64|\n65|Sometimes you just can’t know what will happen without using it and that is essential. Spending too long planning can cause ideas to get confused or get you trapped in a loop where you just make plans worse.  Having simple clear checkpoints is great.\n66|\n67|### Principles\n68|- When planning, factor in points to check certain things and how the plan can be adapted when needed\n69|- Try and create safe ways to test functionality, ie not in prod, when possible as this will allow you to confirm things work.\n70|- Focus on one small change at a time, get tests passing then work on the next element.\n71|- Always design code with the intent it will be changed/replaced soon\n72|- Minimise friction in development even if it is small\n73|- Make change easy, then make the change. IE don’t abstract a single line just because its repeated unless it has some complex logic like a regex.\n46|- Don’t fear repetition of code\n47|- Make sure the code is easily searchable for any given task. If I said modify the task history box in the ui it should  be easy and logical to figure out where that is.\n48|- Use folders as a tool for organising\n49|\n50|## Tested over trusted \n51|\n52|Functionality should not assumed to exist until it is tested and evidenced. “it should work” isn’t always reliable and we want to make sure there are no regressions. \n53|\n54|### Principles\n55|- Try and at least plan what tests you are going to make before you  code a function\n56|- Don’t assume typing is correct until proven, or allow it to fail safe\n57|- Failures should clear transparent and observable, every function doesnt need to intensly check it just needs to report failures accurately\n58|- Tests must be consistent\n59|- Integration test must reflect how a user could want to use the app\n60|- Use the lowest possible level of tests( Ie Unit over api over e2e) for the fastest test cycle\n61|\n62|\n63|## Fast iteration over long planning\n64|\n65|Sometimes you just can’t know what will happen without using it and that is essential. Spending too long planning can cause ideas to get confused or get you trapped in a loop where you just make plans worse.  Having simple clear checkpoints is great.\n66|\n67|### Principles\n68|- When planning, factor in points to check certain things and how the plan can be adapted when needed\n69|- Try and create safe ways to test functionality, ie not in prod, when possible as this will allow you to confirm things work.\n70|- Focus on one small change at a time, get tests passing then work on the next element.\n71|- Always design code with the intent it will be changed/replaced soon\n72|- Minimise friction in development even if it is small\n73|- Make change easy, then make the change. Even if making change easy is hard.\n74|\n75|\n76|\n77|# Inspirations\n78|My principles here are inspired by:\n79|\n80|- Extreme programming Explained by Kent Beck (book)\n81|- Life isn’t binary (book)\n82|- Intent driven design by David whitney (Talk)\n83|\n84|\n85|# Examples\n86|\n87|## Intent Driven descriptions\n88|\n89|### Bad Example\n90|\n91|```js\n92|\n93|const userInOneYearFactory = (name, age, users) => {\n94|\n95|    const user = {name: name , age: age + 1}\n96|\n97|    users.push(user)\n98|  \n99|}\n100|\n101|const list = []\n102|\n103|userFactory(\"Frank\",32,list)\n104|\n105|\n106|```\n107|\n108|## Good example\n109|\n110|```js\n111|\n112|/**\n113|* MARK: calculateAgeNextYear\n114|* @description calculates the age someone will be next year\n115|* @example const usersAgeNextYear = calculateAgeNextYear({ageNow: 3})  \n116|console.log(usersAgeNextYear) // 4\n117|*/\n118|const calculateAgeNextYear = ({ageNow}) => {\n119|  const ageNextYear = ageNow + 1\n120|  \n121|  return ageNextYear\n122|}\n123|\n124|const userObjectsList = []\n125|\n126|const usersName = \"Frank\"\n127|const usersAge = 32\n128|\n129|const usersAgeNextYear = calculateAgeNextYear({ageNow: usersAge})\n130|\n131|userObjectsList.push({name: usersName, age: rounds are append-only, so a failback that generates more questions\n6| *   adds a new block at the bottom instead of rewriting earlier answers.\n7| *\n8| *   Round shape:\n9| *   `{ round, generatedAt, stage, questions: [{ id, type, text, options,\n10| *   required, showIf }], answers: { [qid]: { selected: string[], notes } } }`\n11| *\n12| *   Image questions (`type: \"image\"`) behave like `single` (one favourite out\n13| *   of ≤4) but render generated pictures: the agent writes description\n14| *   `options`, the backend fills the `images[]` array\n15| *   (`{ option, file, status, error? }`), and answers still select by\n16| *   description string — so every validation/completion path below keeps\n17| *   working, and a question whose images are missing or failed simply renders\n18| *   its descriptions instead.\n19| *\n20| *   Conditional questions use a deliberately small `showIf` grammar so agents\n21| *   cannot get confused: `{ questionId, value }` (visible when the referenced\n22| *   answer selected `value`) or `{ questionId, values: [...] }` (visible when\n23| *   any of `values` was selected). Anything else (including the string form\n24| *   `q1 === \"x\"` shown in older drafts) is treated as \"no condition\" by the\n25| *   validator and rejected on write — one object form only.\n26| *\n27| *   A hidden question never blocks completion: `unansweredRequired` skips\n28| *   questions whose `showIf` is not satisfied, and answers already stored for\n29| *   a now-hidden question are preserved untouched.\n30| *\n31| *   An explicitly empty round (`questions: []`) is valid and means \"the agent\n32| *   had good reason to ask nothing\" — it completes immediately (`empty`).\n33| *\n34| * @example parseSurvey('# Survey\\n```survey-json\\n{...}\\n```').rounds.length => 1\n35| ***/\n36|\n37|export const SURVEY_FENCE = \"survey-json\";\n38|\n39|export const QUESTION_TYPES = [\"single\", \"multiple\", \"image\"];\n40|\n41|/***\n42| * MARK: IMAGE_QUESTION_MAX_OPTIONS\n43| * @description Most descriptions one image question may carry (one generated\n44| *   picture per description; the human picks a single favourite).\n45| * @example IMAGE_QUESTION_MAX_OPTIONS => 4\n46| ***/\n47|export const IMAGE_QUESTION_MAX_OPTIONS = 4;\n48|\n49|/***\n50| * MARK: IMAGE_ENTRY_STATUSES\n51| * @description Lifecycle of one generated survey image: `pending` (queued or\n52| *   generating), `ready` (bytes on disk under `file`), `failed` (see\n53| *   `error` — the UI falls back to the written description).\n54| * @example IMAGE_ENTRY_STATUSES.includes('ready') => true\n55| ***/\n56|export const IMAGE_ENTRY_STATUSES = [\"pending\", \"ready\", \"failed\"];\n57|\n58|/***\n59| * MARK: IMAGE_ENTRY_FAILURE_CODES\n60| * @description Machine-readable `code` carried by failed image entries\n61| *   (informational — validation ignores it): `no-key` (no API key saved when\n62| *   the job ran — retried once a key exists), `cap` (per-survey image budget\n63| *   spent), `gen` (the provider call itself failed).\n64| * @example IMAGE_ENTRY_FAILURE_CODES.includes('no-key') => true\n65| ***/\n66|export const IMAGE_ENTRY_FAILURE_CODES = [\"no-key\", \"cap\", \"gen\"];\n67|\n68|/***\n69| * MARK: extractFenceBlocks\n70| * @description Returns the raw text of every ````survey-json```` fenced block\n71| *   in a markdown document, in document order. Fences without the exact\n72| *   `survey-json` language tag are ignored (human prose, other code).\n73| * @example extractFenceBlocks('```survey-json\\n{}\\n```') => ['{}']\n74| * @param {string} markdown\n75| * @returns {string[]}\n76| ***/\n77|export function extractFenceBlocks(markdown) {\n78|\tif (typeof markdown !== \"string\" || markdown === \"\") return [];\n79|\tconst blocks = [];\n80|\tconst pattern = /```survey-json[ \\t]*\\r?\\n([\\s\\S]*?)```/g;\n81|\tlet match;\n82|\twhile ((match = pattern.exec(markdown)) !== null) {\n83|\t\tblocks.push(match[1]);\n84|\t}\n85|\treturn blocks;\n86|}\n87|\n88|/***\n89| * MARK: normalizeRound\n90| * @description Coerces one parsed JSON value into the canonical round shape,\n91| *   filling defaults (`answers: {}`, `required: false`, `showIf: null`) so\n92| *   readers tolerate agent-authored blocks that omit optional fields.\n93| *   Returns null when the value is not a round-like object.\n94| * @example normalizeRound({ round: 1, questions: [] }).round => 1\n95| * @param {*} value - Parsed JSON value from one fence block.\n96| * @param {number} index - Zero-based position (fallback round number).\n97| * @returns {Object|null}\n98| ***/\n99|export function normalizeRound(value, index = 0) {\n100|\tif (!value || typeof value !== \"object\" || Array.isArray(value)) return null;\n101|\tconst questions = Array.isArray(value.questions) ? value.questions : null;\n102|\tif (!questions) return null;\n103|\tconst answers =\n104|\t\tvalue.answers && typeof value.answers === \"object\" && !Array.isArray(value.answers)\n105|\t\t\t? value.answers\n106|\t\t\t: {};\n107|\treturn {\n108|\t\tround:\n109|\t\t\tNumber.isFinite(Number(value.round)) && Number(value.round) > 0\n110|\t\t\t\t? Number(value.round)\n111|\t\t\t\t: index + 1,\n112|\t\tgeneratedAt: typeof value.generatedAt === \"string\" ? value.generatedAt : null,\n113|\t\tstage: typeof value.stage === \"string\" ? value.stage : null,\n114|\t\tquestions: questions.map((q) => normalizeQuestion(q)).filter(Boolean),\n115|\t\tanswers,\n116|\t};\n117|}\n118|\n119|/***\n120| * MARK: normalizeQuestion\n121| * @description Coerces one question descriptor into canonical shape.\n122| *   Returns null for non-objects; `showIf` and `images` are passed through\n123| *   untouched so `validateSurvey` (not the reader) decides whether they are\n124| *   well-formed.\n125| * @example normalizeQuestion({ id: 'q1', text: 'T?', options: ['a'] }).type => 'single'\n126| * @param {*} value\n127| * @returns {Object|null}\n128| ***/\n129|export function normalizeQuestion(value) {\n130|\tif (!value || typeof value !== \"object\" || Array.isArray(value)) return null;\n131|\tconst id = typeof value.id === \"string\" ? value.id.trim() : \"\";\n132|\tconst text = typeof value.text === \"string\" ? value.text : \"\";\n133|\tconst options = Array.isArray(value.options)\n134|\t\t? value.options.map((o) => String(o))\n135|\t\t: [];\n136|\treturn {\n137|\t\tid,\n138|\t\ttype:\n139|\t\t\tvalue.type === \"multiple\"\n140|\t\t\t\t? \"multiple\"\n141|\t\t\t\t: value.type === \"image\"\n142|\t\t\t\t\t? \"image\"\n143|\t\t\t\t\t: \"single\",\n144|\t\ttext,\n145|\t\toptions,\n146|\t\trequired: value.required === true,\n147|\t\tshowIf:\n148|\t\t\tvalue.showIf === undefined || value.showIf === null ? null : value.showIf,\n149|\t\timages: Array.isArray(value.images) ? value.images : [],\n150|\t};\n151|}\n152|\n153|/***\n154| * MARK: parseSurvey\n155| * @description Parses every `survey-json` block in a SURVEY.md document into\n156| *   normalized rounds. Invalid JSON blocks are skipped but reported in\n157| *   `errors` (index + message) so the UI can warn instead of crashing.\n158| * @example parseSurvey('no fences').rounds => []\n159| * @param {string} markdown\n160| * @returns {{ rounds: Array<Object>, errors: Array<Object> }}\n161| ***/\n162|export function parseSurvey(markdown) {\n163|\tconst blocks = extractFenceBlocks(markdown);\n164|\tconst rounds = [];\n165|\tconst errors = [];\n166|\tblocks.forEach((raw, index) => {\n167|\t\tlet parsed;\n168|\t\ttry {\n169|\t\t\tparsed = JSON.parse(raw);\n170|\t\t} catch (err) {\n171|\t\t\terrors.push({ index, message: `round ${index + 1}: invalid JSON (${err.message})` });\n172|\t\t\treturn;\n173|\t\t}\n174|\t\tconst round = normalizeRound(parsed, index);\n175|\t\tif (!round) {\n176|\t\t\terrors.push({ index, message: `round ${index + 1}: not a survey round object` });\n177|\t\t\treturn;\n178|\t\t}\n179|\t\trounds.push(round);\n180|\t});\n181|\treturn { rounds, errors };\n182|}\n183|\n184|/***\n185| * MARK: serializeRound\n186| * @description Serializes one round to indented JSON for embedding in a\n187| *   `survey-json` fence. api/flow/execution/applyRunnerReport.js | head -n 140\",\"description\":\"Show agent guide and flow diffs\"}","output":"Read text file `skills/question-me/SKILL.md`.\n1|---\n2|name: question-me\n3|description: Generate a set of survey questions up‑front for an agent stage, write them to `{{outputFile}}` in the task folder, and flag the stage as awaiting human input. The skill is used to replace iterative “grill‑me” interactions with a single questionnaire.\n4|lastUpdated: 2026-10-29\n5|---\n6|\n7|# Question‑Me (Survey Generator)\n8|\n9|Use this skill when you want an **agent stage** to produce a list of multiple‑choice questions (with an optional free‑form notes field) for a human to answer later. The skill:\n10|\n11|1. **Generates questions** based on the stage’s prompt.\n12|2. **Writes** a `{{outputFile}}` file in the current task’s directory (`docs/tasks/<taskId>/`).\n13|3. **Never overwrites** existing content – it reads the file first and **appends** a new round of questions at the bottom, preserving any prior answers.\n14|4. **Marks the stage as awaiting human input** (task status `waiting_human`) so the UI shows the survey banner and the survey page.\n15|5. Supports **conditional questions** via one simple `showIf` object form: `{ \"questionId\": \"q1\", \"value\": \"Option A\" }` or `{ \"questionId\": \"q1\", \"values\": [\"A\", \"B\"] }`. The UI hides those questions unless the condition is met. No other condition syntax is supported — never write string expressions.\n16|6. **Question ids must be unique across the whole survey** (including every appended round). Re-using an id makes answers ambiguous, so append rounds with fresh ids such as `q5`, `q6`.\n17|\n18|## Expected `{{outputFile}}` format\n19|\n20|The file contains a **machine‑parseable JSON block** wrapped in a fenced code block (`survey-json`). The JSON is the single source of truth; a human‑readable markdown preview is generated from it by the UI.\n21|\n22|```markdown\n23|# Survey – generated by the \"question‑me\" skill\n24|\n25|```survey-json\n26|{\n27|  \"round\": 1,\n28|  \"generatedAt\": \"2026-10-29T13:00:00.000Z\",\n29|  \"stage\": \"{{stageId}}\",\n30|  \"questions\": [\n31|    {\n32|      \"id\": \"q1\",\n33|      \"type\": \"single\",\n34|      \"text\": \"What is the primary security concern?\",\n35|      \"options\": [\"Authentication\", \"Authorization\", \"Data protection\", \"Other\"],\n36|      \"required\": true,\n37|      \"showIf\": null\n38|    },\n39|    {\n40|      \"id\": \"q2\",\n41|      \"type\": \"multiple\",\n42|      \"text\": \"Which regulatory frameworks apply?\",\n43|      \"options\": [\"PCI‑DSS\", \"HIPAA\", \"GDPR\", \"None\"],\n44|      \"required\": false,\n45|      \"showIf\": { \"questionId\": \"q1\", \"value\": \"Data protection\" }\n46|    }\n47|  ],\n48|  \"answers\": {\n49|    \"q1\": { \"selected\": [\"Data protection\"], \"notes\": \"PII in uploads\" }\n50|  }\n51|}\n52|```\n53|\n54|*The UI renders each question as a set of radio‑buttons or check‑boxes with a **Notes** textarea underneath. Fill `generatedAt` with the current UTC time in ISO‑8601 (as above) and `stage` with the stage id already resolved into this prompt (`{{stageId}}`) — never leave a placeholder token in the written file; the backend validates the round and rejects unreadable ones.*\n55|\n56|When the user finishes the survey, the UI updates the `answers` object in‑place (preserving the surrounding JSON) and saves the file.\n57|\n58|### Append‑only behaviour\n59|- If `{{outputFile}}` already exists, the skill **reads** it, determines the next `round` number, and **appends** a new JSON block under a new heading `## Round N`.\n60|- Existing `answers` objects are left untouched.\n61|- The skill must never delete or rewrite previous rounds.\n62|{{#if imageGen}}\n63|## Image questions (generated design examples)\n64|\n65|This stage may also ask **image questions**: the human sees up to 4 generated pictures (UI mocks, logos, …) and picks one favourite. Image generation for this stage runs through the configured provider (`{{imageGen}}`); the backend generates the pictures after you write the survey — you only write detailed descriptions.\n66|\n67|Write an image question like this:\n68|\n69|```survey-json\n70|{\n71|  \"id\": \"q3\",\n72|  \"type\": \"image\",\n73|  \"text\": \"Which dashboard design should we build?\",\n74|  \"options\": [\n75|    \"Dark analytics dashboard, left sidebar navigation, teal accent charts, dense data table, modern SaaS look\",\n76|    \"Light minimal dashboard, top navigation bar, large KPI cards, generous whitespace, friendly rounded corners\"\n77|  ],\n78|  \"required\": true,\n79|  \"showIf\": null\n80|}\n81|```\n82|\n83|Rules:\n84|- `type` is exactly `\"image\"`; `options` holds 1–4 detailed descriptions (each one becomes a picture — write them detailed enough to render a UI mock or logo: layout, palette, key elements, style).\n85|- Answers work like `single`: the human picks one favourite description; the chosen picture is saved into the task folder (`assets/`) and referenced from `{{outputFile}}` for downstream stages to work from.\n86|- Never write an `images` field yourself — the backend owns it (generation status per picture). If generation is unavailable, the survey falls back to showing your descriptions as options, so always make them self-explanatory.\n87|{{/if}}\n88|## How the engine treats the skill\n89|- During stage execution, after the agent returns **success**, the backend inspects the stage’s skill list. If `question-me` is present, it reads `{{outputFile}}` and decides:\n90|  - **Unanswered required questions** (or no `{{outputFile}}` at all) → the task parks with status `waiting_human` instead of auto‑advancing. If generation is unavailable, the survey falls back to showing your descriptions as options, so always make them self-explanatory.\n87|{{/if}}\n88|## How the engine treats the skill\n89|- During stage execution, after the agent returns **success**, the backend inspects the stage’s skill list. If `question-me` is present, it reads `{{outputFile}}` and decides:\n90|  - **Unanswered required questions** (or no `{{outputFile}}` at all) → the task parks with status `waiting_human` instead of auto‑advancing. The task detail page shows the survey banner; the survey page opens at `/tasks/:taskId/survey`.\n91|  - **Explicitly empty round** (`questions: []` — you had good reason to ask nothing) → the run advances normally, no parking.\n92|  - **Already answered** → the run advances normally.\n93|- Submitting the survey (`POST /tasks/:taskId/survey`) merges answers only — questions are never added, removed, or renamed there. A partial save stays parked; a complete submit advances the task to its next stage, which may then read `{{outputFile}}`.\n94|\n95|## Downstream stages\n96|Tell the stage after the survey (e.g. the plan stage) to factor in `{{outputFile}}` — for example: \"Factor in {{outputFile}} into your plan. If there is not enough information, fail the stage with information needed.\" A failback re-runs the question stage, which appends a fresh round at the bottom.\n97|\n98|## Human‑only edge‑cases\n99|- If you genuinely have **no questions**, still write one round with `questions: []` rather than writing no file. An empty round advances without parking; a missing file parks so a human confirms there is nothing to ask (the survey page offers Continue in both cases).\n100|\n101|## UI considerations (mobile & desktop)\n102|- Render each question inside a `<fieldset>`.\n103|- Options are full‑width touch targets; use `type=\"radio\"` for `single` and `type=\"checkbox\"` for `multiple`.\n104|- The **Notes** textarea is optional but always present; on mobile it expands to the full width.\n105|- Conditional visibility is evaluated client‑side; hidden questions are collapsed but their stored answers remain unchanged.\n106|- Accessibility: all inputs have `aria‑label` and are keyboard‑navigable.\n107|\n108|## Configuring the output file\n109|\n110|The output file name is read from the skill configuration. In `KB_config.json`:\n111|\n112|```json\n113|{\n114|  \"keywords\": {\n115|    \"outputFile\": { \"value\": \"SURVEY.md\" },\n116|    \"minQuestions\": { \"value\": \"0\" }\n117|  },\n118|  \"defaults\": { \"mode\": \"direct\" }\n119|}\n120|```\n121|\n122|A stage attachment can override the file name without editing the skill, for\n123|example:\n124|\n125|```json\n126|{ \"name\": \"question-me\", \"config\": { \"outputFile\": \"FEEDBACK.md\" } }\n127|```\n128|\n129|Accepted config keys (canonical first, then aliases): `outputFile`, `surveyFile`,\n130|`surveyFileName`, `fileName`, `targetFile`, `file`. Plain names without an\n131|extension become a `.md` file (`FEEDBACK` → `FEEDBACK.md`); anything else must\n132|already end in `.md`. Path traversal or unsafe names fall back to `SURVEY.md`.\n133|\n134|Multi-stage tasks should give each question stage its own file, e.g.\n135|`FEEDBACK.md`, `SECURITY_QUESTIONARY.md`, `INTENT_SURVEY.md`, while the\n136|default single-survey setup keeps `SURVEY.md`.\n137|\n138|## Suggested minimum question count\n139|\n140|`minQuestions` is a soft prompt hint only; the engine never enforces it. docs/tasks/ef13c0e6-273e-4ce2-8227-7e730db77fb5/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md"},"output":"# Implementation Plan: Image (UI-example) questions for the question-me skill\n\nTask folder: `docs/tasks/ef13c0e6-273e-4ce2-8227-7e730db77fb5/`\nSource request: give the question-me skill an image-question option — agent proposes up to 4 detailed UI/logo\ndescriptions, the survey renders them as generated example images, the human picks one, and the chosen image is\nsaved in the task folder and referenced from SURVEY.md (or equivalent). API key lives in general settings;\nskill config gets an image-gen dropdown (`none` removes the image-gen section entirely, otherwise select a\nprovider). First provider: Muse/Meta image generation, designed for later extension. Key stays server-side.\nPlan scope: planning only — no code is changed in this stage.\n\n## Goal & scope guard\n\n- A new survey question type for image choice. The agent writes up to 4 detailed descriptions; the **backend**\n  generates the images (gateway model — runners/agents never see the key), stores them in the task folder\n  `assets/` directory, and the survey UI renders them as a single-pick image question with a descriptions\n  fallback when generation is unavailable or fails.\n- General (system) settings gains a persisted per-provider API-key store with a new Settings UI section.\n- The question-me skill config gains an `imageGen` keyword (`none` | provider id) rendered as a dropdown in\n  the workflow editor's Skills panel; `none` removes the image-gen section from the agent prompt entirely.\n- Non-goals for this slice: more than one real provider (Muse Image only, behind a registry built for more);\n  per-project keys (shared key only, per q2 default); multiple sizes (one fixed size, per q6 default);\n  video/edit/reference-composition features of Muse Image; changing existing `single`/`multiple` behaviour\n  (byte-identical when `imageGen: none`, which is the default).\n\n## Inputs and survey position\n\n- Grill survey (`SURVEY.md`) is present but `answers` is `{}` — Round 1 (q1–q7) is **unanswered**. Every survey\n  answer below is a provisional default (the options marked Recommended, or the task text where it decides),\n  not a user decision. Re-confirm q1 (provider identity) before locking Phase B.\n- The prior report named in the stage brief (`idea-20261102-005723.md`) is **not present** in this checkout;\n  only `SURVEY.md` exists in the task folder, so no prior findings could be reused beyond the survey itself.\n\n### Survey factored in — provisional defaults (reversible)\n\n| # | Survey question | Provisional decision | Rationale & how it shapes the plan |\n|---|-----------------|----------------------|-------------------------------------|\n| q1 | Which image service first (Muse/Meta)? | **Muse Image (`muse-image-1.0`) via the Meta Model API** (`https://api.meta.ai/v1`), API-key auth | Matches the task text (\"muse/meta image gen interface\"); verified to exist as a developer API in Aug 2026 (see Sources). Exact request schema is pinned in Phase 0 spike; a provider interface + mock provider means no other work blocks on it. If the user names a different service, only the provider adapter changes. |\n| q2 | Where is the image key saved? | **One shared key in general settings** | The Recommended option and the task text agree. Implemented as a new persisted system-level secret store (none exists today — see finding 5) with an env override. |\n| q3 | How do image choices work? | **Up to 4 pictures, pick one favourite** | The Recommended option. New question `type: \"image\"` behaves like `single` (one selection) with image cards instead of radio rows. |\n| q4 | When are pictures created? | **Most reliable: eagerly at park time, in the background** | The Recommended option (\"no preference — most reliable\") plus the task's reliability steer. Backend starts generation when the task parks for survey; images are ready (or failed-with-fallback) before the human opens the page. Survey GET reports per-image status so the UI can show progress if generation is still running. |\n| q5 | Pictures cannot be made? | **Show the written descriptions instead** | The Recommended option. Descriptions are always in the round JSON (the agent writes them), so fallback is free: render option text + a notice, never block answering. |\n| q6 | Picture shapes in v1? | **One fixed size** | The Recommended option. One configured size (square-ish default TBD in Phase 0) for all image questions; no per-question size field in v1. |\n| q7 | How many picture questions per survey? | **Several allowed, each up to 4 pictures** | The Recommended option, with a cost guard: a per-survey image cap (default 12 = 3 full questions) enforced by the backend; questions beyond the cap render descriptions-only with a notice. |\n\n## Research findings (verified in this checkout — big pieces first)\n\n1. **Survey model — `shared/survey.js` (~500+ lines; verified).** Single source of truth shared by backend and\n   frontend: `QUESTION_TYPES = [\"single\", \"multiple\"]`, `normalizeQuestion`, `validateSurvey`, `serializeRound`,\n   `applyAnswers`, `unansweredRequired`, `surveyStatus`. Any new question type must extend normalize + validate +\n   serialize together or rounds will fail validation on write (`appendSurveyRound` / `saveSurveyAnswers` reject\n   invalid rounds and leave the file untouched). `options` are plain strings; answers are `{ selected: string[],\n   notes: string }` subsets of options.\n2. **Survey backend — `api/work/taskSurvey.js` (verified) + routes in `api/work/taskWorkRoutes.js`.**\n   `readSurvey` / `appendSurveyRound` / `saveSurveyAnswers` / `spliceRoundsIntoMarkdown` (byte-preserving answer\n   merge) are the established patterns; `GET /tasks/:id/survey` returns `{ surveyFile, exists, status, rounds,\n   errors, ... }` and `POST` merges answers only. The question-me gate is `resolveSurveyGate` + `readSurvey`,\n   invoked from `api/flow/execution/parkTaskForSurvey.js` (verified, sync function used by both embedded and\n   Runner-report finish paths). Generation must therefore be fire-and-forget-at-park or lazy-on-GET — it cannot\n   be synchronous inside the park call.\n3. **Task image storage + serving already exists — `api/routes/taskImages.js` + `api/work/taskAssets.js`\n   (verified).** Images live in `<cwd>/docs/tasks/<taskId>/assets/`, referenced relatively\n   (`![alt](assets/<name>)`); helpers cover allowlist (`png/jpg/jpeg/gif/webp`), `sanitizeImageName`,\n   `dedupeImageName`, `writeTaskImage`, `listTaskImages`; serving is binary-safe with immutable cache headers\n   at `GET /projects/:id/tasks/:taskId/images/:name`. Generated survey images reuse all of this — no new\n   storage or serving layer needed.\n4. **Skill config pipeline (verified end-to-end).** `skills/question-me/KB_config.json` declares\n   `keywords.{outputFile,minQuestions}` (+ `context`, `defaults.mode`); per-stage overrides live in\n   `stage.skills[i].config` and layer over defaults in `resolveSkillKeywordMap` (`api/skills/skillInjection.js`);\n   substitution is dumb `{{key}}` replacement (`applySkillKeywords`) — **there is no conditional-section\n   mechanism**, so \"none removes the section entirely\" needs a new seam (Phase A1). The workflow editor edits\n   per-stage keyword values in `frontend/src/components/workflow/StageSkillsPanel.jsx` (~1020 lines): kbRef\n   keywords render as cascading dropdowns (precedent for metadata-driven dropdowns), everything else is\n   free-text/JSON — so a metadata-driven provider dropdown follows an existing pattern (Phase A2).\n5. **No persisted system-level secret store exists (verified by grep).** System Settings\n   (`frontend/src/components/settings/SystemSettingsContent.jsx` + `settingsTabs.js`) has persisted tabs\n   (Storage/Notifications/Prompt Layout via their own endpoints) and wireframe tabs (Models/Engine: \"changes\n   here are not saved yet\"). Global config is env-driven and **read-only** (`api/config/schema.js`, served\n   redacted via `GET /status/config` with `secret: true` flags). Per-project settings persist through the\n   project store (`PATCH /projects/:id`). So \"save an API key in general settings\" requires a **new**\n   system-secret store + endpoints + UI section — this is the biggest new-backend piece (Phase A3).\n6. **Survey UI — `frontend/src/components/tasks/SurveyPage.jsx` (577 lines; verified).** Renders rounds via a\n   `QuestionField` component (radio/checkbox + Notes), `showIf` visibility via shared helpers, Save vs\n   Submit-and-advance, `Save answers`/`Submit & continue`/`Continue without questions` buttons. Image questions\n   slot in as a new `QuestionField` variant (image cards + radio semantics + Notes). Existing tests:\n   `SurveyPage.test.jsx`, `SurveyBanner.test.jsx`; canary `canary-e2e/tests/survey-verify.spec.js`.\n7. **Runner trust boundary.** Runners authenticate with join tokens / per-runner credentials (see\n   `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_JOIN_TOKEN` in `api/config/schema.js`) and operate on task docs; the task explicitly says\n   the key must stay in the backend. Decision: **backend gateway** — the runner/agent only writes descriptions\n   into SURVEY.md like any other question text; all provider calls happen server-side. This is also the easiest\n   option: no runner protocol change, no credential distribution, works for embedded runs identically.\n8. **Provider grounding.** Muse Image is Meta Superintelligence Labs' image model, served to developers as\n   `muse-image-1.0` on the Meta Model API (`https://api.meta.ai/v1`, API-key auth, ~$0.01/image announced) and\n   alternatively via fal.ai (`meta/muse-image/text-to-image`). Exact REST schema/auth headers must be verified\n   against Meta's developer docs in the Phase 0 spike (docs move fast; discovery snippets are not a schema).\n\n## Approach — make change easy, then make the change\n\n> Workers before jobs: first create the seams (conditional skill sections, metadata-driven keyword dropdowns,\n> provider registry + mock, persisted key store, survey-model image support), each shippable and tested on its\n> own with zero behaviour change; then wire the feature through them. Research and the riskiest backend piece\n> (secret store + provider contract) come first so later UI work cannot discover a structural blocker.\n\nKey decisions:\n\n- **Backend gateway, not runner generation.** Easiest (no runner protocol/credential work) and most reliable\n  (one code path for embedded + Runner runs; key never leaves the server; retries/timeouts centralised).\n- **Eager background generation at park time.** `parkTaskForSurvey` parks synchronously as today, then\n  fire-and-forget `ensureSurveyImages()` generates missing images, writes them via `taskAssets` helpers, and\n  splices `images[]` status into the round JSON. Survey GET surfaces per-image `ready/pending/failed` so the\n  UI can poll or fall back. Rejected alternative: lazy generation on first survey GET — simpler code, but the\n  human waits on image latency and refresh races are harder; rejected alternative 2: synchronous at park —\n  blocks stage finish on provider latency and risks timeouts.\n- **Descriptions are the durable contract; images are derived artifacts.** The agent writes\n  `type: \"image\"` + ≤4 description `options`; the backend fills `images[]`; answers stay `{ selected, notes }`\n  selecting by description string, so every existing validation/completion path keeps working and q5 fallback\n  is automatic.\n- **Chosen image persistence:** on successful submit/advance, the backend copies the selected image to a stable\n  name (`assets/survey-r<round>-<qid>-chosen.png`) and appends a `## Chosen designs` markdown section to the\n  survey file with `![...](assets/...)` references — satisfying \"saved as an image in the task folder with a\n  reference in SURVEY.md or equivalent\" without disturbing the append-only round JSON.\n\n## Step-by-step workflow (ordered: big/research early)\n\n### Phase 0 — Research spike & contract freeze (blocks everything; no prod code)\n\n1. Verify the Muse Image developer API against Meta's current docs (endpoint, auth header, text-to-image\n   schema, sizes, response bytes/URL, rate limits, pricing). Record the exact pinned contract + doc URL in\n   this file's Sources section. If the Meta Model API is unreachable from the test environment, record fal.ai\n   as the verified fallback path (do not implement it in this slice).\n2. Freeze the round-JSON contract for image questions (proposed; confirm or amend here before Phase A):\n   `{ id, type: \"image\", text, options: [≤4 description strings], required, showIf,\n   images: [{ option: <index>, file: \"assets/<name>\", status: \"pending|ready|failed\", error?: string }] }`.\n   Agent writes everything except `images`; backend owns `images`.\n3. Freeze the `imageGen` keyword contract: KB_config default `\"none\"`; stage override `\"none\"` or a provider\n   id from the registry (`\"muse\"` in v1); unknown values fail safe to `none` + process-log warning.\n4. Freeze the conditional-section syntax for SKILL.md (proposal: `{{#if imageGen}} … {{/if}}` blocks evaluated\n   against the layered keyword map, where `\"none\"`/`\"\"`/missing is falsy). Confirm it composes with the\n   existing unknown-`{{...}}`-preserved guarantee.\n5. Re-confirm q1 (Muse Image vs another service) and the per-survey image cap with the user if reachable;\n   otherwise proceed on the provisional defaults above.\n6. Exit: contract written here; spike code (if any) thrown away or kept only as the mock provider fixture.\n\n### Phase A — Make the change easy (seams; each independently testable, no behaviour change)\n\n- **A1. Conditional skill sections.** Extend `api/skills/skillInjection.js` with the Phase-0 conditional syntax\n  (render/omit blocks from the layered keyword map), keeping byte-identical output for skills without\n  conditionals (guarded by the existing `promptCuration.skills.contract` tests). Unit tests: truthy/falsy/\n  missing/`none` keyword, nested unknowns preserved, size-cap accounting unchanged.\n- **A2. Metadata-driven keyword dropdowns.** Extend `StageSkillsPanel.jsx` so a KB_config keyword entry with\n  UI metadata renders a `<select>` instead of free text. Proposed metadata:\n  `{ \"value\": \"none\", \"description\": \"…\", \"ui\": \"provider-select\", \"providerApi\": \"/api/image-gen/providers\" }`,\n  options fetched from the backend registry (id + label), with static `enum: [...]` as the offline fallback.\n  Unit tests with a mock client; existing free-text/JSON paths untouched.\n- **A3. Provider registry + key store (biggest backend piece).** New `api/imageGen/` module:\n  - `providers.js`: registry interface `{ id, label, generate({prompt, size}) -> Buffer, configured() }`,\n    with `mock` (deterministic fixture PNG, no network) and `muse` (Phase-0 contract) adapters.\n  - `keyStore.js`: per-provider keys in a `0600` JSON file under the KainBain dir (`api/kainbainDir.js`\n    pattern), env override `KAINBAIN_IMAGE_GEN_<PROVIDER>_API_KEY`, keys never logged/returned\n    (follow `shared/redactSecrets.js` + `secret: true` schema conventions).\n  - Routes: `GET /api/image-gen/providers` (id/label/configured only — never keys), `PUT`/`DELETE`\n    `/api/image-gen/providers/:id/key`. Unit + route tests incl. redaction, traversal-safe ids, 0600 perms.\n- **A4. Survey-model image support.** Extend `shared/survey.js`: accept `type: \"image\"` in\n  `normalizeQuestion`/`validateSurvey`/`serializeRound` (options ≤4, non-empty; `images[]` optional,\n  backend-owned, validated when present); single-pick answer semantics identical to `single` (reuse\n  `unansweredRequired`/`applyAnswers` unchanged). Shared tests incl. fixtures for pending/failed/ready.\n- **A5. Round-image splice helper.** Add `updateSurveyImages()` to `api/work/taskSurvey.js` following the\n  `saveSurveyAnswers` pattern (parse → merge `images[]` only → validate → `spliceRoundsIntoMarkdown` →\n  atomic write; rejects leave the file untouched). Unit tests incl. concurrent-edit conflicts.\n\n### Phase B — Make the change (wire the feature)\n\n- **B1. Skill config + prompt.** Add the `imageGen` keyword to `skills/question-me/KB_config.json`\n  (default `none`, provider-select UI metadata) and an `{{#if imageGen}}` section to `skills/question-me/SKILL.md`\n  documenting the image-question format (type/options ≤4/descriptions guidance: \"detailed enough to render a\n  UI mock or logo\"). Verify prompt output with `imageGen: none` is byte-identical to today.\n- **B2. Settings UI.** New System Settings tab `Images` (`settingsTabs.js` + new `ImageGenSection.jsx`,\n  persist-immediately pattern like Prompt Layout): per-provider rows showing configured/not-configured,\n  key save (password input) / clear, and a \"test\" button that runs the mock-or-real generation dry-run.\n  Unit tests with mock client.\n- **B3. Generation job at park.** In the park path (`parkTaskForSurvey.js` callers), after a successful park,\n  fire-and-forget `ensureSurveyImages({ cwd, project, taskId, surveyFile, stage })`: resolve provider from the\n  stage's `imageGen` config (default `none` → no-op); skip when provider unconfigured (leave `pending`→`failed`\n  with `no-key` so the UI falls back to descriptions per q5); enforce per-survey cap; generate via registry\n  with timeout + 1 retry; write PNGs with `writeTaskImage` (sanitized `survey-r<round>-<qid>-<i>.png` names);\n  splice `images[]` via A5; log to the process log. Unit + integration tests with the mock provider\n  (no network), incl. Runner-report finish path parity.\n- **B4. If the user names a different service, cost is one new\n  adapter (~1 file) + Phase-0 re-verification.\n- **New secret store is new attack surface.** Mitigated by 0600 file perms, env override, redaction\n  conventions, and never returning keys from any endpoint (configured-boolean only). No encryption-at-rest in\n  v1 (same posture as other local secrets — record if this needs revisiting).\n- **Image latency at park.** Mitigated by fire-and-forget + per-image timeout + UI polling/fallback; the park\n  itself never waits on the provider.\n- **Cost.** Muse Image ~$0.01/image announced; worst case 12 images/survey ≈ $0.12. Per-survey cap + no\n  regeneration of `ready` images bound this. No budget UI in v1.\n- **Scope creep (sizes, multi-pick, per-project keys, more providers).** Explicitly out of scope; the\n  registry + keyword metadata are the extension points, documented as follow-ups, not built now.\n\n## Sources\n\n- [Introducing Muse Image and Muse Video (ai.meta.com)](https://ai.meta.com/blog/introducing-muse-image-muse-video-msl/)\n  — inspected 2026-11-02: confirms Muse Image as Meta Superintelligence Labs' image model with developer\n  availability. Exact REST schema to be pinned from Meta's developer docs in Phase 0 (not in this post).\n- Meta Model API base URL (`https://api.meta.ai/v1`), model id (`muse-image-1.0`), fal.ai availability and\n  $0.01/image pricing appear only in discovery snippets so far — **unverified**, must be confirmed against\n  primary docs in Phase 0 before the adapter is written.\n- **As-built (implementation stage):** the Muse adapter in `api/imageGen/providers.js` was written against\n  an assumed OpenAI-compatible contract (`POST {base}/images/generations` with `model`/`prompt`/`size`/`n`/\n  `response_format: b64_json`, `Bearer` auth, `b64_json`-or-`url` response) with a base-URL override\n  (`KAINBAIN_IMAGE_GEN_MUSE_BASE_URL`). This assumption is **still unverified against a live call** — no\n  real key was available in the build environment. Before relying on Muse generation in production, run\n  one live generation via `POST /settings/image-gen/providers/muse/test` (or the Images settings tab's\n  test button) and correct the adapter if Meta's actual schema differs; only that one file should change.\n","partials":"# Implementation Plan: Image (UI-example) questions for the question-me skill\n\nTask folder: `docs/tasks/ef13c0e6-273e-4ce2-8227-7e730db77fb5/`\nSource request: give the question-me skill an image-question option — agent proposes up to 4 detailed UI/logo\ndescriptions, the survey renders them as generated example images, the human picks one, and the chosen image is\nsaved in the task folder and referenced from SURVEY.md (or equivalent). API key lives in general settings;\nskill config gets an image-gen dropdown (`none` removes the image-gen section entirely, otherwise select a\nprovider). First provider: Muse/Meta image generation, designed for later extension. Key stays server-side.\nPlan scope: planning only — no code is changed in this stage.\n\n## Goal & scope guard\n\n- A new survey question type for image choice. The agent writes up to 4 detailed descriptions; the **backend**\n  generates the images (gateway model — runners/agents never see the key), stores them in the task folder\n  `assets/` directory, and the survey UI renders them as a single-pick image question with a descriptions\n  fallback when generation is unavailable or fails.\n- General (system) settings gains a persisted per-provider API-key store with a new Settings UI section.\n- The question-me skill config gains an `imageGen` keyword (`none` | provider id) rendered as a dropdown in\n  the workflow editor's Skills panel; `none` removes the image-gen section from the agent prompt entirely.\n- Non-goals for this slice: more than one real provider (Muse Image only, behind a registry built for more);\n  per-project keys (shared key only, per q2 default); multiple sizes (one fixed size, per q6 default);\n  video/edit/reference-composition features of Muse Image; changing existing `single`/`multiple` behaviour\n  (byte-identical when `imageGen: none`, which is the default).\n\n## Inputs and survey position\n\n- Grill survey (`SURVEY.md`) is present but `answers` is `{}` — Round 1 (q1–q7) is **unanswered**. Every survey\n  answer below is a provisional default (the options marked Recommended, or the task text where it decides),\n  not a user decision. Re-confirm q1 (provider identity) before locking Phase B.\n- The prior report named in the stage brief (`idea-20261102-005723.md`) is **not present** in this checkout;\n  only `SURVEY.md` exists in the task folder, so no prior findings could be reused beyond the survey itself.\n\n### Survey factored in — provisional defaults (reversible)\n\n| # | Survey question | Provisional decision | Rationale & how it shapes the plan |\n|---|-----------------|----------------------|-------------------------------------|\n| q1 | Which image service first (Muse/Meta)? | **Muse Image (`muse-image-1.0`) via the Meta Model API** (`https://api.meta.ai/v1`), API-key auth | Matches the task text (\"muse/meta image gen interface\"); verified to exist as a developer API in Aug 2026 (see Sources). Exact request schema is pinned in Phase 0 spike; a provider interface + mock provider means no other work blocks on it. If the user names a different service, only the provider adapter changes. |\n| q2 | Where is the image key saved? | **One shared key in general settings** | The Recommended option and the task text agree. Implemented as a new persisted system-level secret store (none exists today — see finding 5) with an env override. |\n| q3 | How do image choices work? | **Up to 4 pictures, pick one favourite** | The Recommended option. New question `type: \"image\"` behaves like `single` (one selection) with image cards instead of radio rows. |\n| q4 | When are pictures created? | **Most reliable: eagerly at park time, in the background** | The Recommended option (\"no preference — most reliable\") plus the task's reliability steer. Backend starts generation when the task parks for survey; images are ready (or failed-with-fallback) before the human opens the page. Survey GET reports per-image status so the UI can show progress if generation is still running. |\n| q5 | Pictures cannot be made? | **Show the written descriptions instead** | The Recommended option. Descriptions are always in the round JSON (the agent writes them), so fallback is free: render option text + a notice, never block answering. |\n| q6 | Picture shapes in v1? | **One fixed size** | The Recommended option. One configured size (square-ish default TBD in Phase 0) for all image questions; no per-question size field in v1. |\n| q7 | How many picture questions per survey? | **Several allowed, each up to 4 pictures** | The Recommended option, with a cost guard: a per-survey image cap (default 12 = 3 full questions) enforced by the backend; questions beyond the cap render descriptions-only with a notice. |\n\n## Research findings (verified in this checkout — big pieces first)\n\n1. **Survey model — `shared/survey.js` (~500+ lines; verified).** Single source of truth shared by backend and\n   frontend: `QUESTION_TYPES = [\"single\", \"multiple\"]`, `normalizeQuestion`, `validateSurvey`, `serializeRound`,\n   `applyAnswers`, `unansweredRequired`, `surveyStatus`. Any new question type must extend normalize + validate +\n   serialize together or rounds will fail validation on write (`appendSurveyRound` / `saveSurveyAnswers` reject\n   invalid rounds and leave the file untouched). `options` are plain strings; answers are `{ selected: string[],\n   notes: string }` subsets of options.\n2. **Survey backend — `api/work/taskSurvey.js` (verified) + routes in `api/work/taskWorkRoutes.js`.**\n   `readSurvey` / `appendSurveyRound` / `saveSurveyAnswers` / `spliceRoundsIntoMarkdown` (byte-preserving answer\n   merge) are the established patterns; `GET /tasks/:id/survey` returns `{ surveyFile, exists, status, rounds,\n   errors, ... }` and `POST` merges answers only. The question-me gate is `resolveSurveyGate` + `readSurvey`,\n   invoked from `api/flow/execution/parkTaskForSurvey.js` (verified, sync function used by both embedded and\n   Runner-report finish paths). Generation must therefore be fire-and-forget-at-park or lazy-on-GET — it cannot\n   be synchronous inside the park call.\n3. **Task image storage + serving already exists — `api/routes/taskImages.js` + `api/work/taskAssets.js`\n   (verified).** Images live in `<cwd>/docs/tasks/<taskId>/assets/`, referenced relatively\n   (`![alt](assets/<name>)`); helpers cover allowlist (`png/jpg/jpeg/gif/webp`), `sanitizeImageName`,\n   `dedupeImageName`, `writeTaskImage`, `listTaskImages`; serving is binary-safe with immutable cache headers\n   at `GET /projects/:id/tasks/:taskId/images/:name`. Generated survey images reuse all of this — no new\n   storage or serving layer needed.\n4. **Skill config pipeline (verified end-to-end).** `skills/question-me/KB_config.json` declares\n   `keywords.{outputFile,minQuestions}` (+ `context`, `defaults.mode`); per-stage overrides live in\n   `stage.skills[i].config` and layer over defaults in `resolveSkillKeywordMap` (`api/skills/skillInjection.js`);\n   substitution is dumb `{{key}}` replacement (`applySkillKeywords`) — **there is no conditional-section\n   mechanism**, so \"none removes the section entirely\" needs a new seam (Phase A1). The workflow editor edits\n   per-stage keyword values in `frontend/src/components/workflow/StageSkillsPanel.jsx` (~1020 lines): kbRef\n   keywords render as cascading dropdowns (precedent for metadata-driven dropdowns), everything else is\n   free-text/JSON — so a metadata-driven provider dropdown follows an existing pattern (Phase A2).\n5. **No persisted system-level secret store exists (verified by grep).** System Settings\n   (`frontend/src/components/settings/SystemSettingsContent.jsx` + `settingsTabs.js`) has persisted tabs\n   (Storage/Notifications/Prompt Layout via their own endpoints) and wireframe tabs (Models/Engine: \"changes\n   here are not saved yet\"). Global config is env-driven and **read-only** (`api/config/schema.js`, served\n   redacted via `GET /status/config` with `secret: true` flags). Per-project settings persist through the\n   project store (`PATCH /projects/:id`). So \"save an API key in general settings\" requires a **new**\n   system-secret store + endpoints + UI section — this is the biggest new-backend piece (Phase A3).\n6. **Survey UI — `frontend/src/components/tasks/SurveyPage.jsx` (577 lines; verified).** Renders rounds via a\n   `QuestionField` component (radio/checkbox + Notes), `showIf` visibility via shared helpers, Save vs\n   Submit-and-advance, `Save answers`/`Submit & continue`/`Continue without questions` buttons. Image questions\n   slot in as a new `QuestionField` variant (image cards + radio semantics + Notes). Existing tests:\n   `SurveyPage.test.jsx`, `SurveyBanner.test.jsx`; canary `canary-e2e/tests/survey-verify.spec.js`.\n7. **Runner trust boundary.** Runners authenticate with join tokens / per-runner credentials (see\n   `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_JOIN_TOKEN` in `api/config/schema.js`) and operate on task docs; the task explicitly says\n   the key must stay in the backend. Decision: **backend gateway** — the runner/agent only writes descriptions\n   into SURVEY.md like any other question text; all provider calls happen server-side. This is also the easiest\n   option: no runner protocol change, no credential distribution, works for embedded runs identically.\n8. **Provider grounding.** Muse Image is Meta Superintelligence Labs' image model, served to developers as\n   `muse-image-1.0` on the Meta Model API (`https://api.meta.ai/v1`, API-key auth, ~$0.01/image announced) and\n   alternatively via fal.ai (`meta/muse-image/text-to-image`). Exact REST schema/auth headers must be verified\n   against Meta's developer docs in the Phase 0 spike (docs move fast; discovery snippets are not a schema).\n\n## Approach — make change easy, then make the change\n\n> Workers before jobs: first create the seams (conditional skill sections, metadata-driven keyword dropdowns,\n> provider registry + mock, persisted key store, survey-model image support), each shippable and tested on its\n> own with zero behaviour change; then wire the feature through them. Research and the riskiest backend piece\n> (secret store + provider contract) come first so later UI work cannot discover a structural blocker.\n\nKey decisions:\n\n- **Backend gateway, not runner generation.** Easiest (no runner protocol/credential work) and most reliable\n  (one code path for embedded + Runner runs; key never leaves the server; retries/timeouts centralised).\n- **Eager background generation at park time.** `parkTaskForSurvey` parks synchronously as today, then\n  fire-and-forget `ensureSurveyImages()` generates missing images, writes them via `taskAssets` helpers, and\n  splices `images[]` status into the round JSON. Survey GET surfaces per-image `ready/pending/failed` so the\n  UI can poll or fall back. Rejected alternative: lazy generation on first survey GET — simpler code, but the\n  human waits on image latency and refresh races are harder; rejected alternative 2: synchronous at park —\n  blocks stage finish on provider latency and risks timeouts.\n- **Descriptions are the durable contract; images are derived artifacts.** The agent writes\n  `type: \"image\"` + ≤4 description `options`; the backend fills `images[]`; answers stay `{ selected, notes }`\n  selecting by description string, so every existing validation/completion path keeps working and q5 fallback\n  is automatic.\n- **Chosen image persistence:** on successful submit/advance, the backend copies the selected image to a stable\n  name (`assets/survey-r<round>-<qid>-chosen.png`) and appends a `## Chosen designs` markdown section to the\n  survey file with `![...](assets/...)` references — satisfying \"saved as an image in the task folder with a\n  reference in SURVEY.md or equivalent\" without disturbing the append-only round JSON.\n\n## Step-by-step workflow (ordered: big/research early)\n\n### Phase 0 — Research spike & contract freeze (blocks everything; no prod code)\n\n1. Verify the Muse Image developer API against Meta's current docs (endpoint, auth header, text-to-image\n   schema, sizes, response bytes/URL, rate limits, pricing). Record the exact pinned contract + doc URL in\n   this file's Sources section. If the Meta Model API is unreachable from the test environment, record fal.ai\n   as the verified fallback path (do not implement it in this slice).\n2. Freeze the round-JSON contract for image questions (proposed; confirm or amend here before Phase A):\n   `{ id, type: \"image\", text, options: [≤4 description strings], required, showIf,\n   images: [{ option: <index>, file: \"assets/<name>\", status: \"pending|ready|failed\", error?: string }] }`.\n   Agent writes everything except `images`; backend owns `images`.\n3. Freeze the `imageGen` keyword contract: KB_config default `\"none\"`; stage override `\"none\"` or a provider\n   id from the registry (`\"muse\"` in v1); unknown values fail safe to `none` + process-log warning.\n4. Freeze the conditional-section syntax for SKILL.md (proposal: `{{#if imageGen}} … {{/if}}` blocks evaluated\n   against the layered keyword map, where `\"none\"`/`\"\"`/missing is falsy). Confirm it composes with the\n   existing unknown-`{{...}}`-preserved guarantee.\n5. Re-confirm q1 (Muse Image vs another service) and the per-survey image cap with the user if reachable;\n   otherwise proceed on the provisional defaults above.\n6. Exit: contract written here; spike code (if any) thrown away or kept only as the mock provider fixture.\n\n### Phase A — Make the change easy (seams; each independently testable, no behaviour change)\n\n- **A1. Conditional skill sections.** Extend `api/skills/skillInjection.js` with the Phase-0 conditional syntax\n  (render/omit blocks from the layered keyword map), keeping byte-identical output for skills without\n  conditionals (guarded by the existing `promptCuration.skills.contract` tests). Unit tests: truthy/falsy/\n  missing/`none` keyword, nested unknowns preserved, size-cap accounting unchanged.\n- **A2. Metadata-driven keyword dropdowns.** Extend `StageSkillsPanel.jsx` so a KB_config keyword entry with\n  UI metadata renders a `<select>` instead of free text. Proposed metadata:\n  `{ \"value\": \"none\", \"description\": \"…\", \"ui\": \"provider-select\", \"providerApi\": \"/api/image-gen/providers\" }`,\n  options fetched from the backend registry (id + label), with static `enum: [...]` as the offline fallback.\n  Unit tests with a mock client; existing free-text/JSON paths untouched.\n- **A3. Provider registry + key store (biggest backend piece).** New `api/imageGen/` module:\n  - `providers.js`: registry interface `{ id, label, generate({prompt, size}) -> Buffer, configured() }`,\n    with `mock` (deterministic fixture PNG, no network) and `muse` (Phase-0 contract) adapters.\n  - `keyStore.js`: per-provider keys in a `0600` JSON file under the KainBain dir (`api/kainbainDir.js`\n    pattern), env override `KAINBAIN_IMAGE_GEN_<PROVIDER>_API_KEY`, keys never logged/returned\n    (follow `shared/redactSecrets.js` + `secret: true` schema conventions).\n  - Routes: `GET /api/image-gen/providers` (id/label/configured only — never keys), `PUT`/`DELETE`\n    `/api/image-gen/providers/:id/key`. Unit + route tests incl. redaction, traversal-safe ids, 0600 perms.\n- **A4. Survey-model image support.** Extend `shared/survey.js`: accept `type: \"image\"` in\n  `normalizeQuestion`/`validateSurvey`/`serializeRound` (options ≤4, non-empty; `images[]` optional,\n  backend-owned, validated when present); single-pick answer semantics identical to `single` (reuse\n  `unansweredRequired`/`applyAnswers` unchanged). Shared tests incl. fixtures for pending/failed/ready.\n- **A5. Round-image splice helper.** Add `updateSurveyImages()` to `api/work/taskSurvey.js` following the\n  `saveSurveyAnswers` pattern (parse → merge `images[]` only → validate → `spliceRoundsIntoMarkdown` →\n  atomic write; rejects leave the file untouched). Unit tests incl. concurrent-edit conflicts.\n\n### Phase B — Make the change (wire the feature)\n\n- **B1. Skill config + prompt.** Add the `imageGen` keyword to `skills/question-me/KB_config.json`\n  (default `none`, provider-select UI metadata) and an `{{#if imageGen}}` section to `skills/question-me/SKILL.md`\n  documenting the image-question format (type/options ≤4/descriptions guidance: \"detailed enough to render a\n  UI mock or logo\"). Verify prompt output with `imageGen: none` is byte-identical to today.\n- **B2. Settings UI.** New System Settings tab `Images` (`settingsTabs.js` + new `ImageGenSection.jsx`,\n  persist-immediately pattern like Prompt Layout): per-provider rows showing configured/not-configured,\n  key save (password input) / clear, and a \"test\" button that runs the mock-or-real generation dry-run.\n  Unit tests with mock client.\n- **B3. Generation job at park.** In the park path (`parkTaskForSurvey.js` callers), after a successful park,\n  fire-and-forget `ensureSurveyImages({ cwd, project, taskId, surveyFile, stage })`: resolve provider from the\n  stage's `imageGen` config (default `none` → no-op); skip when provider unconfigured (leave `pending`→`failed`\n  with `no-key` so the UI falls back to descriptions per q5); enforce per-survey cap; generate via registry\n  with timeout + 1 retry; write PNGs with `writeTaskImage` (sanitized `survey-r<round>-<qid>-<i>.png` names);\n  splice `images[]` via A5; log to the process log. Unit + integration tests with the mock provider\n  (no network), incl. Runner-report finish path parity.\n- **B4. Survey UI.** `SurveyPage.jsx` `QuestionField` variant for `type: \"image\"`: image cards (served from\n  the existing task-images endpoint) with single-select radio semantics + Notes; states for pending\n  (skeleton + \"generating…\", lightweight poll of GET survey), failed/missing (description options + notice\n  per q5), and empty-provider (`imageGen: none` but agent wrote image questions → descriptions with a hint).\n  Reuse shared `isQuestionVisible`/`selectedValues` so `showIf` keeps working. Component tests + headless\n  screenshot of each state.\n- **B5. Chosen-image persistence.** On submit/advance with image answers, copy the selected file to\n  `assets/survey-r<round>-<qid>-chosen.png` and append the `## Chosen designs` reference section to the\n  survey file (markdown only — round JSON untouched). Route tests: chosen file exists, reference resolves,\n  idempotent re-submit, multi-file surveys (`outputFile` variants) each get their own section.\n\n### Phase C — Assurance, docs, hardening\n\n- **C1. Validation gate.** Full `npm run test:unit` (api + frontend) green; `npm run lint`; docs checks\n  (`npm run docs:check` — JSDoc examples, doc links); one-function-per-file and duplicate-settings guards if\n  touched. No narrowing of existing suites; new tests live next to the code they cover.\n- **C2. No long-lived servers\n  (per stage guidance — isolated headless runners / mock fixtures only).\n- **C3. If the user names a different service, cost is one new\n  adapter (~1 file) + Phase-0 re-verification.\n- **New secret store is new attack surface.** Mitigated by 0600 file perms, env override, redaction\n  conventions, and never returning keys from any endpoint (configured-boolean only). No encryption-at-rest in\n  v1 (same posture as other local secrets — record if this needs revisiting).\n- **Image latency at park.** Mitigated by fire-and-forget + per-image timeout + UI polling/fallback; the park\n  itself never waits on the provider.\n- **Cost.** Muse Image ~$0.01/image announced; worst case 12 images/survey ≈ $0.12.
